changed.title: The 4 by 4 bipartite graph with mask 60 is represented on the one-a-side promise by an AND/OR/NOT circuit of fan-in two with at most 4 gates
changed.statement: ∃ C : PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Circuit, PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.FanInTwo C ∧ C.size ≤ 4 ∧ PEqualNP.Represents.Represents (fun u v : Fin 4 => (60 : ℕ).testBit (4 * u.val + v.val)) C
changed.unlocks: A witness prices the gate saving from negation on mask 60. Compare its shared and negated wires with the checked AND/OR minimum for the same graph.
changed.sketch: Encode the 16 promised input pairs as wire truth tables. Start with the 4 row masks and 4 column masks. For each of at most 4 gates choose earlier wires and AND, OR or NOT. Order binary operands to remove duplicates. Match every output bit to mask 60. Among circuits of this size at least one NOT is needed by the checked AND/OR floor. Return a gate list and replay all 16 output bits.

changed.title: Every Boolean square can be rematched into few groups with constant diagonal blocks
changed.statement:
∀ (n m : ℕ), 0 < m → m^2*4^m ≤ n →
  ∀ G : Fin n → Fin n → Bool,
    ∃ (π : Equiv.Perm (Fin n)) (group : Fin n → Fin (2*(n/m))),
      ∀ (x y z w : Fin n), group x = group y → group x = group z → group x = group w →
        G x (π y) = G z (π w)
changed.unlocks: constructs a rematching and partition with few monochromatic diagonal squares
changed.context: While at least m4^m rows and columns remain, take 2m rows. For each in turn keep columns carrying its more frequent bit. At least m columns survive. At least m selected rows used the same bit, giving a constant m by m block. Pair its rows and columns and remove both sets. The blocks number at most floor(n/m), and fewer than m4^m≤floor(n/m) unpaired rows remain. Pair these as singleton groups. Complementary pairs of equal sizes extend the matching to all labels.

changed.title: A rank-one field-linear map can agree somewhere with every prescribed multiplier exactly when the reciprocals avoid zero in their affine span
changed.statement:
∀ (E K : Type) [Field E] [Field K] [Algebra E K] [FiniteDimensional E K]
    (S : Finset K), (0 : K) ∉ S →
  ((∃ C : K →ₗ[E] K, Module.finrank E (LinearMap.range C) ≤ 1 ∧
    ∀ z ∈ S, ∃ x : K, x ≠ 0 ∧ C x = z*x) ↔
    (0 : K) ∉ affineSpan E ((fun z : K => z⁻¹) '' (↑S : Set K)))
changed.unlocks: characterizes prescribed nonzero field multipliers that a single correction of rank at most one can meet
changed.context: For nonempty S write the nonzero rank-one map as C(x)=u f(x). The equation C(x)=zx for x nonzero implies f(u/z)=1 after cancelling f(x). Thus the reciprocal set lies on one affine hyperplane avoiding zero. Conversely if its affine span omits zero, a linear functional L takes value one there. Annihilate the direction space and normalize at a basepoint. Take C(x)=L(x) times the field unit and x=1/z. The empty set uses the zero map. Allow 1 to 3 hours.

changed.title: It is false that: One-a-side promise: the 4 by 6 bipartite graph with mask 268222 has a fan-in-two AND/OR circuit of at most 9 gates
changed.unlocks: Proving it shows that a listed statement is false.
changed.context: The literal negation of another statement of the fleet; a counterexample to that statement proves it.
changed.sketch: Keep columns 0,1,5 and rows 0,1,2. Delete columns 2,3,4 and row 3 one at a time. Each live duplicate costs at least one first-reader gate by fixing its wire to zero. Reorder the three rows as 0,2,1 and the three columns as 1,0,5, then pad both banks with a zero site. The result is four-by-four mask 293. A size-nine witness gives size five, contradicting checked L-meta-5506.

changed.title: The second highest joint agreement count for quadratic predictors of disjoint triple products
changed.statement:
∀ (m : ℕ), 2 ≤ m →
  let r := 3
  let V := Fin m × Fin r
  let W := V → Bool
  let low := fun (f : W → Bool) =>
    ∃ terms : Finset (Finset V), (∀ mon ∈ terms, mon.card < r) ∧
      ∀ x, f x = (((terms.filter (fun mon => ∀ a ∈ mon, x a = true)).card % 2) == 1)
  let prodBit := fun (x : W) (i : Fin m) => decide (∀ j : Fin r, x (i,j) = true)
  let hits := fun (P : Fin m → W → Bool) (e : Fin m → Bool) =>
    ((Finset.univ : Finset W).filter (fun x =>
      ∀ i, xor (prodBit x i) (P i x) = e i)).card
  ∀ e : Fin m → Bool,
    (∀ P, (∀ i, low (P i)) → hits P e < 7^m → hits P e ≤ 43 * 7^(m-2)) ∧
    (∃ P, (∀ i, low (P i)) ∧ hits P e = 43 * 7^(m-2) ∧ hits P e < 7^m)
changed.unlocks: Gives the best possible individual cover contribution below a translation cell, allowing predictors to read every block.
changed.context: Normalize one failing triple by flipping bits to remove its local quadratic pairs. Multiply its remaining correction by one plus each local bit. An exterior quadratic forces all three single-bit leading multiples. A mixed term forces two distinct local pairs on the same exterior bit, whose allowed multiples are disjoint. Either removes at least 6 times 7^(m-2) previously allowed monomials. One mixed bit product on two triples gives 28 plus 15 allowed inputs and each remaining triple contributes seven.

changed.title: Known result rebuilt. Guarded width bounds give a b-way Promise-Ball-SAT search within radius r
changed.statement:
∀ (n b r : Nat), 0 < b →
  let V := Fin n
  let Point := V → Bool
  let Clause := Finset (V × Bool)
  let sat := fun (formula : Finset Clause) (x : Point) =>
    ∀ c ∈ formula, ∃ lit ∈ c, x lit.1 = lit.2
  ∀ (clauses : List Clause) (center : Point),
    let F := clauses.toFinset
    let bad := fun (x : Point) (c : Clause) => ∀ lit ∈ c, x lit.1 ≠ lit.2
    let vars := fun (c : Clause) => c.image Prod.fst
    let state := fun (flipped : Finset V) (v : V) =>
      if v ∈ flipped then !(center v) else center v
    let run := fun (choices : Fin r → Fin b) =>
      (List.finRange r).foldl (fun used step =>
        let c := (clauses.find? (fun d => decide (bad (state used) d))).getD ∅
        let options := ((vars c) \ used).sort (· ≤ ·)
        let picked := options[ (choices step).val ]?
        used ∪ picked.toList.toFinset) (∅ : Finset V)
    (∀ c ∈ F, (vars c).card ≤ b+1) →
    (∀ c ∈ F, bad center c → (vars c).card ≤ b) →
    ((∃ y : Point, sat F y ∧ ((Finset.univ : Finset V).filter (fun i => y i ≠ center i)).card ≤ r) ↔
      (∃ choices : Fin r → Fin b, sat F (state (run choices))))
changed.unlocks: Rebuilds the bounded Promise-Ball-SAT branching step with both width promises guarding the equivalence.
changed.context: Maintain agreement of flipped bits with a chosen nearby model. A false clause has an unflipped variable on which the current word differs from that model. If it was false initially it has at most b variables. If it was true initially, at least one of its at most b+1 variables is already flipped. Hence a valid branch selects the useful variable and reduces distance by one. Once satisfied, all remaining steps are idle. Conversely the procedure flips at most r bits.
